digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center binding store and reconciliation
propositions: When a Jira issue moves between projects, its KEY changes but its numeric id remains immutable; bindings keyed on the KEY become stale and fail to resolve when the moved_issue_key table is not updated by third-party automation, silently orphaning the binding from a live issue.
The absence probe treats a stale key that 404s as evidence the issue is gone and retires the binding, even though the issue still exists and is resolvable by its numeric id.

The binding store must capture and persist the numeric jira_id alongside the key, and when a key lookup misses, retry by id and re-key the binding to the issue's current key while maintaining the reverse index in the same operation.

This fix is additive to the existing key-keyed store paths, leaving Cloud-facing semantics and all existing jira_key-taking methods unchanged, with no migration required for pre-existing bindings lacking the recorded id.

On a real DC 8.17.1 instance, GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey} for a moved issue returns 200 with the new key in the body, so the 404 recovery path functions as a safety net for the case where moved_issue_key table updates fail.
The id fallback must not fire when the old key still resolves normally, preserving happy-path performance and avoiding redundant lookups.
